subject: Bridge / decision log: LedgerPay latency spike and mitigation plan
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: High p50/p95 spikes impacting LedgerPay - proposed bridge

Quick summary: starting 09:05 PT we began seeing a sustained p95 latency increase for LedgerPay's gen and embedding routes. p50 jumped from ~45ms -> 160ms, p95 from ~220ms -> ~1.1s. Throughput for their customer pool is down ~18% (retries up).

Affected endpoints: /v1/generate (primary), /v1/embeddings (background jobs).
Metrics snapshot attached (incident_snapshot_20270629.pdf).

Immediate asks: 
- Can we stand up a 30m bridge now (propose 09:30 PT) to triage and agree customer comms?
- Engineering mitigation options: temporary fallback to rwin-7b-ql8 variant (lower latency, slightly lower quality), enable targeted prefix KV cache warmup for LedgerPay keys, or apply short burst throttle for non-critical background jobs.

My recommendation: enable model fallback + KV warmup as first action (low-risk), then consider throttling background embeddings if no improvement in 10-15m.

I'll bring logs, scheduler traces, and a quick packet of kernel metrics to the bridge.

Attachments: incident_snapshot_20270629.pdf

Ben
Ben Carter
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, alex@ledgerpay.com
Cc: ops@ledgerpay.com
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High p50/p95 spikes impacting LedgerPay - proposed bridge

Thanks Ben — good catch.

I can host the bridge at 09:30 PT as Ben suggested. Agenda for the 20m session: 
- Quick signal review (Ben)
- Short term mitigations and risk (Karthik)
- Customer-facing message and ask (me)
- Action owners + decision log

Product asks we need clarity on before messaging: 
1) Quality vs latency tradeoff — are we comfortable offering fallback to rwin-7b-ql8 for 30-60 minutes if it cuts p95 by >50%? Is that an engineering toggle only or do we need product sign-off?
2) SLA/credit posture — potential for a P95 breach for LedgerPay; do we pre-clear a goodwill credit (50% of one hour usage) or wait until post-mortem?
3) Do we want to proactively throttle non-critical embeddings to buy headroom (customers may see delayed background tasks)?

Please confirm owners for each decision on the bridge. I'll draft a customer note once we have the mitigation decision.

Marissa Cole
Product Manager, Core Serving
Redwood Inference
From: Alex Turner <alex@ledgerpay.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@ledgerpay.com
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 09:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High p50/p95 spikes impacting LedgerPay - proposed bridge

Thanks for the heads up — we can jump on the 09:30 bridge. Impact here: checkout tokenization calls are timing out intermittently; we saw a ~12% increase in declined transactions during the 09:05-09:20 window. Background fraud scoring jobs are also queuing.

Immediate request from LedgerPay: if a short-term fallback reduces customer-visible failures, please proceed — our primary ask is to keep checkout success high. We can handle small quality downgrades for 30-60 minutes if that stabilizes latency.

I'll be joined on the bridge by Sara (ops@ledgerpay.com).

—Alex
Alex Turner
Head of Platform, LedgerPay
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: alex@ledgerpay.com, ops@ledgerpay.com
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Decision log and customer follow-up — LedgerPay latency incident (final)

Summary of actions taken (decision log):
- 09:33 PT: Enabled model fallback for LedgerPay traffic to rwin-7b-ql8 (traffic slice) — immediate p95 improvement from ~1.1s -> ~380ms, p50 ~45ms -> ~70ms.
- 09:38 PT: Warmed prefix KV cache for top 12 LedgerPay keys (kv_cache_warmup_plan.txt) — small additional improvement for repeated sessions.
- 09:50 PT: Temporarily throttled non-critical background embeddings for LedgerPay (30m window) to restore headroom.

Customer-facing note (sent to LedgerPay): "We've observed and mitigated an elevated latency condition affecting generation and embedding flows between 09:05–10:00 PT. We applied a short-term model fallback and cache warmup which restored service for interactive checkout flows. Our team will continue monitoring and is running a post-incident review. Follow-up: a formal RCA and any SLA adjustments within 72 hours." (I sent the note at 10:05 PT).

Product/engineering asks for roadmap/prioritization (post-incident):
- Short-term: prioritize a low-latency model variant for high-QPS interactive routes (owner: Marissa).
- Mid-term: automated per-customer fallback policies + safer canary rollout for fallback (owner: Karthik).
- Long-term: expand cache prewarm controls and per-customer cache capacity visibility (owner: SRE/Ben).

SLA/credits: we offered LedgerPay a goodwill credit equal to 50% of one hour's billed usage; Alex accepted (recorded in HS-123456). We will surface this in the billing sync.

Attachments: incident_snapshot_20270629.pdf, kv_cache_warmup_plan.txt

Thanks team — we should capture this in the weekly ops review and assign the roadmap tickets.

Grace O'Connor
Director, Customer Reliability (interim)
Redwood Inference
